Constructions & algorithms · 2025

The Transformer Cookbook

Andy Yang, Christopher Watson, Anton Xue, Satwik Bhattamishra, Jose Llarena, William Merrill, Emile Dos Santos Ferreira, Anej Svete, and David Chiang

A collection of recipes for turning algorithms into transformer weights.

Read the paper ↗Companion video ↓

The idea, briefly

This paper brings together techniques for explicitly constructing transformers that carry out algorithms. Its recipes cover arithmetic in feed-forward layers and routing information through attention.

The collection offers a shared reference for constructions scattered across the literature. It is a useful place to begin when you want to understand how a computation can be represented inside the architecture.

Editorial overview based on the paper’s abstract. Reading suggestions below are editorial guidance.

Why spend time here?

For the moment when you want to build a transformer construction, and need a place to start.

A way into the paper

  • Choose one operation you already understand and follow how the paper encodes it.
  • Keep track of the architectural assumptions each recipe needs before combining constructions.
Keep in mind

An explicit construction describes what chosen parameters can compute. Whether training discovers those parameters is a separate question.
